The company:

AAK is one of the world’s leading producers of vegetable oils and speciality fats, that are used in everything from creams to infant nutrition. At AAK-s production site in Aarhus, we specialize in the production of oils and fats for the chocolate and confectionery industries.

We produce and sell our products business-to-business exclusively. Our Customer references span from small, local manufacturers to large, global companies within our different markets. AAK Denmark A/S is centrally located on the south harbor in Aarhus, and today we have approximately 240 competent and motivated employees. We focus greatly on safety, as well as showing he right safety-measures. Being a part of maintaining the safety culture is a very important part of our daily work and routine.

We develop and provide value-adding vegetable oil solutions in close collaboration with our customers, enabling them to achieve long lasting business results.

We do so through our in-depth expertise in oils & fats within food applications, working with a wide range of raw materials and broad process capabilities.

Through our unique co-development approach, we bring together our customers’ skills and know-how with our capabilities and mindset. By doing so, we solve customer specific needs across many industries – Chocolate & Confectionery, Bakery, Dairy, Special Nutrition, Foodservice, Personal Care, and more.

The position:

HR Specialist.

Do you have a broad HR admin profile?

Are you firmly grounded in system- and process competencies?

We are looking for a professional, strong and experienced HR Specialist with experience from international production environments. You focus on structure, processes and IT tools, which can contribute to the development and execution of our admin, development & recruitment efforts. You will become part of an exciting development process in a global corporation, which is one of the industry’s most significant players.

The position:

With reference to the Head of HR, you are given the responsibility to build and further develop our plans and efforts within HRM systems as well as data management and extraction.

You will be responsible for introducing and implementing Cornerstone (AAK People), Mercer, Tableau and other relevant HR IT tools as well as working extensively with job profiles, job descriptions, revising employment contracts, employee handbook and policies etc.

You have solid experience with processes and best practice in recruitment and onboarding, which takes place across our sites inland and abroad. You have extensive experience with recruitment processes and manage them independently.

It is crucial you possess a strong business understanding and your passion for HR is driven by the needs and values of the business.

It is a small and operational HR team, which must be able to execute at all levels within the entire group.

Responsibilities:

• Participate in the development and planning of HR tasks in general and in the areas of responsibility as well as reporting

• Introducing, incorporating and supporting the users with Cornerstone, Mercer, Tableau and other HRM IT tools into the organization

• Subject Matter Expert regionally on eg recruitment or other areas of the HR lifecycle

• Contribute with job descriptions/profiles, contracts and policies as well as updating the employee handbook

• Recruitment excellence: Recruitment and introduction/onboarding

• Organizing and evt. conducting internal trainings

• Assist in designing and updating GDPR processes

• Back-up of monthly reports to managers, social security etc.

The candidate:

Systematic, structured and business-oriented – focus on execution and outcome

There are many ways into this role. Your background may be a relevant mercantile education such as cand.merc., HD-O or equivalent, but most important is your “toolbox”, experiences from a similar role in an international production company and not least your personality.

You can balance the “thinker and doer” – in other words, you like to create structures and processes, most often based on IT tools and to execute and create results in the business. You manage to convert the strategic vision for HR into concrete efforts with structure and action which create results and work in practice.

Furthermore, you are a role model for the values, the good colleague and collaboration across the organization. You are a team player and ensure everyone, as a team, reach our goals.

You are based on the site in Aarhus with a few travel days per year. You speak and write Danish and English on a professional level. In addition, you are a seasoned SAP and Microsoft Office user. You are offered a challenging position in a globally oriented corporation with high ambitions. You will become part of a dedicated team with an open and positive attitude.

It’s an exciting time to join Tactile. We're a diverse team of storytellers, puzzle enthusiasts, and casual mobile game creators. Our story began in 2008 in the heart of beautiful Copenhagen, and since then, we have experienced continuous growth, establishing ourselves as one of the largest gaming companies in Denmark. In more recent years, we have been scaling fast, in large part thanks to the success of a little game called Lily’s Garden. Now we’re on a mission to solidify our position as one of the leaders in creating out-of-the-ordinary casual puzzle games.

With more than 350 talented individuals, we are a mix of over 50 nationalities and 43% women. We truly appreciate the richness of different experiences and perspectives that Tactilers bring to the game. This is why we foster a lean organisational culture, in which each individual is encouraged to take responsibility, be open, and grow in their own way. We pride ourselves on cultivating a studio environment that avoids crunch, fosters your skills regardless of your discipline, and provides a space for you to be creative alongside other passionate and invested storytellers.

🚀 Your role & impact:

We're currently growing our Core team and are on the lookout for another Product Designer to join our team of talented engineers.

The Core team builds the internal tools behind Tactile own LiveOps, Marketing and Data operations, the backbone of our studio. We're looking for a second Product Designer to join Joy and our engineers in designing business-critical tools that every team at Tactile depends on.

This role is based in our Copenhagen office.

How we design:

• Our tools are data-heavy: dashboards, large tables, complex filters, multi-step workflows. Static mockups can't show how they behave with real data, so we prototype first, in code. We use Claude Code and agentic workflows to build working prototypes, and those prototypes are what we hand off to developers. Figma is still where we sketch and brainstorm

• AI amplifies our design. It doesn't do design for us. It lets us take on complex workflows that used to get skipped because they took too much effort

• Quality is not up for debate. We know what good looks like, and we don't ship slop

• Our product design philosophies are inspired by Vercel, Linear and GitHub

This is roughly how we work today. It isn't strict, and we're open to what you bring. Here's a talk that captures our thinking.

Okay, let’s get a little bit more specific. Here’s what you’ll be doing on the day-to-day:

• Research, design and prototype interfaces for our internal tools, then hand working prototypes off to developers

• Work with your team who use our tools to simplify their workflows

• Use AI to explore, iterate and prototype efficiently, while you stay responsible for every design decision and not outsource creative thinking.

• Evolve and contribute to our design system and processes

• We don't have a big UX team, and that's on purpose. You'll work every day with Product Managers, Frontend and Backend engineers, Artists, Game Programmers. We believe good products come from working across disciplines, so we care about the end product, not design operations

What we’re looking for:

• Hands-on experience with technical B2B products: dashboards, tables, filters, dense interfaces

• You care more about the end product than about design process, and you thrive working across disciplines

• Comfortable contributing directly to projects via PRs to improve designs or UX without waiting for programmers to implement them

• Experience in designing with Claude Code or similar agentic tools

• Real openness to agentic workflows, without an "AI produces slop" mindset

• Comfort prototyping in code, or a strong drive to learn

• A sharp eye for high design craft, quality, and candour when something isn't good enough

You'll make us extra excited if you also have:

• Experience in using Figma/Figma Make or similar design tools

• Programmer background, comfortable diving into fronted code if necessary

• Know-how of shadcn, Untitled UI or similar SaaS UI libraries

What’s in it for you?

🌆 Beautiful office space with probably the best view in Copenhagen

🩺 Pension and private health insurance

💻 A chance to work with the latest tools and technology

📚 Opportunities for individual growth with development talks as well as workshops, books and courses

🌮 Daily, healthy organic breakfast and lunch prepared by our professional chefs in-house

🥳 Social activities, including game nights, book club, Friday bar and more

🔍 Free Danish lessons with our in-house Danish teacher

Our interview process

Submit your application via the fill-in form at the top of this page. This is the easiest and fastest way to get in touch with our recruiters. We foster an inclusive culture and accessible workplace and want to make sure we provide everyone with the same opportunities for success. This is why we encourage you to apply regardless of your gender, sexuality, age, nationality, neurodiversity or disability. We review applications based on competencies and experience, so please do tell us about your favorite projects and technologies.

After we review your application, you can expect to go through the following conversations:

☕ Introductory coffee chat, primarily to ensure that we’re aligned on the scope of the role and that all of your questions are answered.

🧪 In person technical interview (mix of design whiteboarding and designing with AI) with Joy, your future product design colleague, and Gab, Core Team Lead.

💜 The final conversation will be with your future team, to discuss if you’re aligned on values and ways of working.

We are thorough in our hiring process, as it's essential to us that we select new Tactilers carefully - just as it is vital to ensure that we are the right place for you.

We want to ensure you have a great candidate experience whilst in our recruitment process. We will do everything within reason to ensure that your interview takes place in an environment that fairly and accurately assesses your skills. If you need assistance or accommodation, please let us know.

We look forward to receiving your application! 👋

jobs.occupation: Senior Process Automation Engineer in DCS at Novo Nordisk Engineering
jobs.description:
Senior Process Automation Engineer in DCS, Novo Nordisk Engineering

Do you want to be a part of NNE’s all-time largest Process Automation team? We are looking for colleagues to join our fantastic company, where we have the aspiration of becoming best in class within Automation Solutions for Pharmaceutical Engineering.

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

You will be working in an enthusiastic Process Automation team with more than 80 colleagues in Denmark. Globally, the Process Automation team has more than 200 employees.

The Process Automation team works with consultancy, design & development, implementation and validation of Automation solutions for the Pharma and Biotech industries. Our work is project based, and currently we are looking into an exciting pipeline of large data driven, greenfield plants with modular/scalable designs.

We are skilled in a broad range of process areas within API production e.g. fermentation, recovery and purification, utility, and cleaning systems. And the solutions we provide to our customers are always based on a deep understanding of the customers’ production processes – and if standard components can’t do the job, we develop our own.

How you might spend your days

As a DCS Senior Process Automation Engineer, you’ll be:

• Advising customers on their application process solutions

• Design developing, programming, commissioning, qualifying, FAT, SAT, UAT and Handover of applications for Distributed Control Systems (DCS)

• Interacting with process experts and colleagues with expertise in surrounding systems and equipment like MES, Historian systems, instruments, production equipment etc.

• Developing and optimizing automation methods and strategies to meet our customers’ needs and sharing working knowledge with colleagues and partners

• Forming the basis of automation strategies and architectures to support our sister departments internationally and expand NNE’s Process Automation engagement

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you:

• Understand your colleagues’ individual and cultural difference

• Are aware of your surroundings and able to flag any concerns

• Are agile and able to prioritize urgent tasks

• Are team-oriented and able to collaborate on team projects

• Are reliable, curious and eager to learn

• Are appreciative of feedback, because it contributes to your growth

What you bring to the role

In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• You have 6+ years or more of working experience and hold a degree as an engineer, ideally within electrical, automation, process or marine engineering

• You have 4 years or more of working experience with PCS/DCS Application development (for example ABB 800xA or ABB SattLine), working in GMP/GAMP environment or with execution of Automation projects

• Knowledge of batch production is valued

• You find the complexity of the GMP/GAMP environment exciting

Life at NNE

NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer here.

Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

Deadline of application is 13th December 2026

Questions before applying? Send us a quick text to arrange a convenient time to chat. Contact Manager Christian Ljørring on +45 30 79 29 08 or Manager Rasmus Sølbeck Hansen +45 31 91 89 30

Please note:

• We only accept applications submitted through our online recruitment system

• You do not need to attach a cover letter, but please include a few sentences about why you are applying in your resume or CV

• We invite to interviews on a running basis.

Fair hiring:

At NNE, we are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all job applicants. To maintain fairness, we request that you refrain from including a personal photo in your CV.

Are you passionate about product data and the systems that turn it into consistent, high-quality experiences everywhere it's used? Do you enjoy the technical challenge of connecting complex data flows across platforms? Do you thrive on making product information easy to find, understand, and trust—for customers and for AI? If so, we might have the perfect opportunity for you!

Pandora's team is looking for a Product Manager to own our Product Information Management (PIM) practice. PIM is central to our architecture, syndicating product data to ecommerce, marketplaces, retail, and marketing systems, so you'll work at the intersection of data architecture, content quality, and discoverability.

As our new Product Manager, you'll own the product strategy and delivery for our PIM platform, with InRiver preferred as our PIM technology. You'll work closely with data, engineering, and content teams to define the data model, govern data quality, and ensure product information flows correctly to every downstream channel.

This role is critical to how our products are found and understood—not just by customers on our own site, but increasingly by AI-driven answer engines and generative search. You'll balance strategic roadmap planning with hands-on technical execution, vendor management, and continuous improvement of our data model.

Help Write Our Next Chapter - Job Responsibilities:

• Own the product roadmap and backlog for our PIM platform, ensuring the data model and architecture support both business and technical needs

• Design and optimize data flows between PIM and downstream systems (ecommerce, marketplaces, DAM, ERP), working closely with engineering

• Partner with content, SEO, and marketing teams to structure and enrich product information for Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)

• Manage vendor relationships, including roadmap alignment, issue escalation, and feature adoption

• Monitor data quality, syndication performance, and platform health, identifying optimization opportunities and driving continuous improvement

• Stay ahead of trends in PIM, product data architecture, and AI-driven discovery, bringing forward strategic recommendations

We would love if you could bring:

• 5+ years of experience in product management, data platforms, or PIM—ideally within ecommerce or product content operations

• Technical understanding of PIM architecture, data modeling, and system integrations (APIs, ETL, syndication)

• Experience with InRiver or similar PIM platforms preferred

• Experience optimizing product information for AEO and GEO—structured data, schema markup, and content formats that AI systems and search engines can parse

• Experience writing clear product requirements and managing backlogs in tools like JIRA

• Analytical mindset with a focus on measuring data quality and discoverability impact

• Excellent stakeholder management skills—you can navigate between technical and business teams with ease

• Familiarity with data privacy regulations (GDPR, consent management) is a plus

We know that great talent comes from different backgrounds and experiences. If this role excites you and you can see yourself bringing many of these skills to the team, we’d love to hear your story!

Meet the People Behind the Sparkle

You’ll join our Product Management team, alongside colleagues in Copenhagen and Baltimore, working in a collaborative and international environment. Reporting directly to the Director, Product Management, you’ll work closely with teams across e-commerce, stores, retail technology, brand, marketplaces and local markets, giving you broad exposure across Pandora and plenty of opportunity to collaborate across the business.

Further Information:

Global Career Band: This role is a Manager, Band 4B, individual contributor position.

Be Part of Something Beautiful

At Pandora, we’re crafting more than jewellery. We’re creating the future of an iconic global brand. You’ll work from our Digital & Technology Hub in Copenhagen alongside talented colleagues from around the world, helping shape the digital experiences, platforms, and technologies that support millions of customers and employees every day. From our LEED Gold-certified workplace to our commitment to sustainability, innovation, and craftsmanship, Pandora offers an environment where you can do meaningful work, grow your career, and make a lasting impact.

You will be working out of our beautiful Digital & Technology site in Copenhagen, in a rapidly growing environment of highly skilled and experienced colleagues, which is a key initiative that goes along with Pandora’s ambitions. Besides our inspiring workplace design, we’re proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This reflects our commitment to using natural resources responsibly and creating a space that is professional, dynamic, comfortable, and uniquely Pandora. The result is a workplace that is innovative, collaborative and inspirational, delivering a true Pandora experience to everyone who works here or comes to visit.

FPRT is a Danish-based defense technology company, part of the international Fire Point Group — a fast-growing ecosystem born out of Ukraine’s innovation and resilience. The group was founded by engineers and entrepreneurs who, during the first months of the full-scale war, decided to use their expertise to create advanced defense technologies — including long-range drones and precision systems.

About FPRT

FirePoint Rocket Technology is building a new advanced defence manufacturing facility in Denmark. As we grow towards 300+ employees, we are looking for a hands-on Payroll & HR Operations Specialist to establish reliable people processes and support our transition to a multi-shift production environment.

Reporting to the CHRO, you will work closely with Finance, managers and external payroll and benefits providers. This is an opportunity to shape HR operations from an early stage, not simply maintain existing processes.

What you’ll do

• Coordinate the monthly Danish payroll process, checking salaries, shifts, overtime, allowances and payroll data with our external provider.

• Own accurate time and attendance administration in WorkLinq, working with managers to resolve discrepancies.

• Manage essential HR administration, including contracts, employee changes, pension and benefits coordination, and offboarding.

• Keep employee records and HR systems accurate, organised and compliant with Danish requirements and collective agreements.

• Improve everyday HR processes and reporting as the workforce grows, supporting a potential future transition to in-house payroll.

What we’re looking for

• 3-5+ years of hands-on experience with Danish payroll and HR administration; manufacturing or shift-based experience is an advantage.

• Working knowledge of Danish employment, tax, pension and payroll practices, including collective agreements.

• Confidence using payroll, HR and time-registration systems; experience with WorkLinq or similar tools is welcome.

• Strong attention to detail, numerical accuracy and a practical, service-minded approach.

• Strong language skills in Danish and English, oral and written

Why join FPRT?

• Build scalable payroll and HR operations for a new high-tech manufacturing site.

• Have direct impact on the employee experience and how a growing company operates.

• Work with an international team on a project supporting European security and defence.

• Competitive compensation and a new facility in Vojens.

Interested? We would be pleased to hear from candidates who enjoy combining accurate execution with building better ways of working.

Practical Information

• Full-time position with an immediate start.

• Location: Vojens, Denmark.

• Interviews are conducted on an ongoing basis, so please submit your application as soon as possible.

• Temp-Team is assisting FPRT with this recruiment so during the initial phases of the recruitment process will be done by Temp-Team and all contact must go via Temp-Team.

Temp-Team

Temp-Team A/S is a national recruitment and staffing agency with eight local departments in Denmark. We have 45 years of experience within staffing and cover a wide range of industries. We focus on delivering high quality and a close personal contact to candidates and clients.

Temp-Team is a part of JuhlerGroup – an international group of recruitment agencies.

jobs.occupation: Business Continuity Manager - Business Impact & Criticality
jobs.description:
The position is based in Roskilde or Warsaw at BEC Financial Technologies' headquarters. The position is organizationally anchored in Service Integration & Security with reference to the Head of Projects & Continuity.

The Service Integration & Security area is responsible for strengthening BEC’s operational resilience and ensuring that critical business services can continue through disruption. We work closely with business areas, banking specialists, risk and compliance functions, and technology stakeholders to establish a shared understanding of business criticality, dependencies, continuity requirements, and recovery priorities.

As Business Continuity Manager, you will lead and develop BEC’s Business Impact Analysis and business criticality processes. You will engage with business owners across BEC to identify critical services and processes, assess the consequences of disruption, clarify dependencies, and define proportionate continuity and recovery requirements. The role requires strong business understanding, facilitation skills, and the ability to translate banking needs and regulatory expectations into clear priorities and practical actions.

At BEC, we prefer to collaborate often in the office, while also offering the opportunity to work remotely on average up to 1 day per week.

Primary tasks and responsibilities include:

Continuity & resilience framework:

• Developing and maintaining BEC’s business continuity management framework with a clear business and customer perspective

• Owning the governance and methodology for Business Impact Analysis and business criticality assessments

• Ensuring that continuity priorities and requirements reflect customer impact, banking obligations, financial exposure, regulatory expectations, and operational dependencies

• Supporting the development and maintenance of business continuity plans and ensuring alignment with relevant standards and regulation

Business Impact Analysis (BIA) ownership & execution:

• Planning, facilitating, and driving Business Impact Analyses across BEC’s business areas and shared functions

• Helping business owners identify critical customer services, products, processes, and activities, including the impact of disruption over time

• Facilitating consistent criticality assessments and supporting management decisions on priorities, tolerances, and continuity requirements

• Identifying and documenting key dependencies on people, suppliers, facilities, information, applications, and other business services

• Maintaining the BIA and criticality methodology, governance, templates, guidance, quality criteria, and review cycle

• Consolidating results into management insight for BEC’s most critical services, business impacts, dependencies, and resilience priorities

Coordination & stakeholder engagement:

• Building strong relationships with business owners, banking specialists, risk and compliance functions, service owners, and senior stakeholders

• Leading workshops and interviews that turn business knowledge into clear, evidence-based impact and criticality assessments

• Challenging assumptions constructively and creating alignment where business priorities, regulatory requirements, and operational capabilities differ

• Translating business continuity needs into clear requirements for relevant operational and technology stakeholders without being the technical solution owner

Validation****, exercises & continuous improvement:

• Validating BIA and criticality outcomes through business reviews, continuity exercises, incidents, and organizational changes

• Facilitating business-focused continuity and crisis exercises that test decision-making, priorities, and cross-functional coordination

• Using lessons learned and stakeholder feedback to improve the continuity framework, BIA process, and organizational readiness

Governance, reporting & insight:

• Preparing clear management reporting on business criticality, BIA coverage, key risks, dependencies, gaps, and improvement priorities

• Providing decision support and business insight that help management prioritize resilience investments and continuity actions

To succeed you will have:

• Solid experience with business continuity management, Business Impact Analysis, operational resilience, or a comparable business-focused discipline

• Practical experience facilitating BIAs, criticality assessments, workshops, or other cross-organizational business processes

• Strong stakeholder-management and facilitation skills, with confidence engaging business owners and senior stakeholders

• A structured and analytical approach, including the ability to assess business impacts, challenge input, identify dependencies, and create a coherent enterprise view

• The ability to translate complex business, risk, and regulatory matters into clear requirements, decisions, and practical actions

• A proactive and collaborative mindset with the ability to drive progress without formal authority

• Clear written and spoken English communication skills

It’s nice-to-have:

• Experience from a bank, mortgage-credit institution, financial infrastructure provider, or another regulated financial-services organization

• Knowledge of relevant continuity and operational-resilience expectations, such as DORA or ISO 22301

• Experience with process management, business architecture, or governance in a complex organization

The role will offer:

• A key role in strengthening BEC’s operational resilience and continuity capabilities

• High visibility across the organization and interaction with senior stakeholders

• The opportunity to shape and evolve BEC’s continuity and BIA practices

• A collaborative environment with strong professional expertise

• A role with tangible impact on BEC’s ability to operate under disruption

Be your best self with BEC's benefits!

We offer a diverse range of benefits for our employees. Here are just a few of them.

• Professional development budget

• Healthy, varied lunch and fruit in the canteen

• Active staff associations: yoga, cycling, go-karting, games, bowling etc.

• Pension scheme

• Health and dentist insurance

• Referral bonus

What does the recruitment process look like?

• Screening call: Let's chat and see if we're a match

• Meet your future manager and team: See who you'll be working closely with.

• Personality and cognitive test: Let's learn more about you.

• Meet our talent partner and your future manager once more: Get feedback on your test results.

• Time to sign the contract: We're ready to welcome you to BEC!

If you have any questions related to the position, please contact Head of Projects & Continuity, Kim Bastholm on +45 61 56 76 10.

Dalea · BioInnovation Institute, Copenhagen · Full-time

Build full-stack AI agents for science, with freedom, room to be creative, and real ownership, in a lively startup in Copenhagen.

An AI agent is only as useful to a scientist as the data it can see and trust. Dalea gives research labs structured data with full provenance, and we want AI co-scientists that do real scientific work on top of it. You'll own the AI side of that.

What you'll own

• 
The agent harness and the framework for AI co-scientist agents, from architecture to the workflows they run.

• 
Our MCP integrations, which give agents access to lab data with a traceable record of what they do.

• 
Model choices: following the field, testing new models against what labs actually need, and adopting what works.

• 
How we evaluate AI quality.

• 
The infrastructure the AI runs on: inference, model serving and agent execution.

• 
Full-stack work wherever the AI needs deeper integration with the platform, and help elsewhere when the team needs it.

What you bring

Must-haves

• 
You've designed and built an LLM agent system used in production, and made the architecture decisions yourself.

• 
Strong full-stack TypeScript (React, Next.js or close equivalents), and you're comfortable in Python.

• 
You've owned the direction of a technical area, including a significant rework.

• 
You've shipped quickly in a small team or an early-stage product.

Nice to have (none of them required)

MCP servers or clients, agent frameworks or harness tooling (open source counts)

Tools for scientists, or a background in bioinformatics, computational biology or AI for science

• 
Mastra or another TypeScript agent framework

• 
Open-weight models, through inference APIs or self-hosting

• 
Kubernetes

• 
Systems where provenance or audit trails matter

You don't need lab or biology knowledge, a PhD or Danish. Hands-on, shipped work counts more than research or publications. If you match the must-haves, apply, even if you have none of the nice-to-haves.

Our stack

TypeScript, Next.js and React. Python for our MCP service. An agent harness built on Mastra. Docker Compose and Kubernetes, hosted on Scaleway.

How we work

Our dev team is the two founders plus up to three new developers, led by our CTO. We discuss progress and priorities closely and continuously, and we expect you to take part: share ideas early, argue for what you think is right, and change course when the evidence says so.

You won't need permission to fix what's broken, and what you build reaches production quickly. We work together at BioInnovation Institute 3–5 days a week. We're building the team and the way we work, and that happens best in person.

About Dalea

Dalea is a data management platform for biology and lab workflows. Experiments, structured data, samples and inventory sit in one place, with full data provenance. Everything a lab builds in Dalea can be packaged and shared, so we're building a GitHub for life science: labs publish and reuse each other's workflows instead of rebuilding them from scratch. We work with biotech startups, academic labs, pharma R&D and CROs.

Timing and our funding round

This position depends on our current funding round closing, which we expect in February/March 2027. We can make a conditional offer before then, and we'll be open with you about the timing throughout the process.

Apply here with your LinkedIn profile, your CV and short answers to a few questions. No cover letter needed.

A data platform for life science research, where experiments, data and workflows stay structured, traceable and easy to share. Dalea is a data management platform for research in biotech, pharma and academic labs. Scientists keep experiments, structured data, samples and inventory in one place, with full data provenance, in tools that feel familiar to anyone coming from Excel and Word. Today, much of that work is scattered across spreadsheets, personal computers and paper notebooks. Results are hard to find and harder to trust, so teams often re-run experiments rather than track down the ones they’ve already done. Think of it as a GitHub for life science. The same structured, traceable data is what lets AI agents work reliably on real lab data. Dalea is built for regulated research. It has a full audit log, 21 CFR Part 11 and EU Annex 11 compliant infrastructure, and full provenance for everything that happens in the platform. It’s hosted in the EU. We’re a small team at BioInnovation Institute in Copenhagen, working with biotech startups, academic labs, pharma R&D teams and CROs.

Dalea · BioInnovation Institute, Copenhagen · Full-time·

Starts when our funding round closes.

Keep a Part 11 and Annex 11 compliant lab data platform secure, reliable and trusted, and own the infrastructure it runs on.

We ask pharma and biotech teams to trust a young company with their most valuable research data. That's a big decision, and they're right to be careful. Dalea already has the safeguards. You'll keep them strong, improve them, and make them easy to verify.

What you'll own

• 
The infrastructure: Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Scaleway, CI/CD, monitoring and backups.

• 
Security: access control, encryption, logging and incident response.

• 
Our GxP setup, which is already built: a full audit log, 21 CFR Part 11 and EU Annex 11 compliant infrastructure, W3C PROV provenance for every entity and operation, rollback engines, and export to machine-readable regulatory formats. You'll audit it, maintain it and make it better.

• 
Our ISO 27001 certification and the controls behind it.

• 
Controlled releases, and validation support for customers who run GxP work in Dalea.

• 
Making trust verifiable: clear security and compliance documentation, and joining customer reviews when the questions get technical.

What you bring

Must-haves

• 
You've owned production infrastructure and deployment (containers, CI/CD, cloud) for a system holding sensitive data.

• 
Hands-on security engineering: access control, encryption, logging and incident response.

• 
Hands-on experience with ISO 27001 or SOC 2, or with GxP and regulated software (computer system validation, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11). One of the two is enough.

• 
You've built and maintained production platform software in a small team or early product where you made decisions.

Nice to have (none of them required)

• 
Experience with both compliance areas above

• 
Vendor audits by pharma customers

• 
Part 11 or Annex 11 systems in practice

• 
Provenance or lineage systems (W3C PROV)

• 
Customer security questionnaires

• 
Kubernetes

• 
TypeScript or Python

You don't need deep frontend skills, lab or biology knowledge, a PhD or Danish. If you match the must-haves, apply, even if you have none of the nice-to-haves.

Our stack

TypeScript, Next.js and React. Python for our MCP service. An agent harness built on Mastra. Docker Compose and Kubernetes, hosted on Scaleway.

How we work

Our dev team is the two founders plus up to three new developers, led by our CTO. We discuss progress and priorities closely and continuously, and we expect you to take part: share ideas early, argue for what you think is right, and change course when the evidence says so.

You won't need permission to fix what's broken, and what you build reaches production quickly. We work together at BioInnovation Institute 3–5 days a week. We're building the team and the way we work, and that happens best in person.

About Dalea

Dalea is a data management platform for biology and lab workflows. Experiments, structured data, samples and inventory sit in one place, with full data provenance. Everything a lab builds in Dalea can be packaged and shared, so we're building a GitHub for life science: labs publish and reuse each other's workflows instead of rebuilding them from scratch. We work with biotech startups, academic labs, pharma R&D and CROs.

Timing and our funding round

This position depends on our current funding round closing, which we expect in February/March 2027. We can make a conditional offer before then, and we'll be open with you about the timing throughout the process.

Location: BioInnovation Institute, Copenhagen, on-site 3–5 days a week. You'll need to live in the Copenhagen area or be willing to move here. We're happy to hear from people relocating within the EU.

Start: when the round closes

Apply here with your LinkedIn profile, your CV and short answers to a few questions. No cover letter needed.

Data is becoming one of the most important foundations for Blue Water’s future. This is a rare opportunity to join at a stage where you can influence and shape the outcome.

As our new Data Architect, you will help shape how data flows across Blue Water. You will establish the principles, models and standards that enable data to be understood, trusted and used consistently across a global organisation. Your work will influence major business initiatives and help create the foundation for technologies and capabilities we have yet to introduce.

This is where you make a difference

From there, you will play a central role in defining the target-state data architecture and building the roadmap to get there. This includes developing conceptual and logical data models, establishing architectural principles and guiding decisions around critical business data and system ownership.

You will also help shape the architecture behind our future Data Platform, ensuring we have the right foundations for metadata, lineage, data quality, security and governance. Along the way, you will review solution designs, challenge assumptions when needed and act as a trusted sparring partner for architects, project teams and business stakeholders. Key responsibilities include:

• Defining and maintaining Blue Water’s enterprise data architecture, standards and modelling principles

• Supporting strategic transformation initiatives, including BlueCore, by ensuring alignment with agreed architectural principles

• Translating business requirements and data definitions into scalable and implementable data models

• Guiding internal teams and external partners on data-related architecture decisions

What you bring

You have experience working with data architecture, data modelling or solution design in complex enterprise environments. You understand that good architecture is not about drawing perfect diagrams. It is about creating practical solutions that balance business needs, technology realities and long-term sustainability. Essential skills:

• Experience with data architecture, data modelling or solution design across multiple systems or business domains

• Experience with cloud data platforms and integration architecture

• SAP S/4HANA experience, particularly around Business Partner data

• Strong communication skills and the ability to explain technical topics to different audiences

• Professional proficiency in English

It is an advantage if you also have experience with:

• Data engineering, integration or enterprise architecture

• Master data management, metadata, lineage and data quality disciplines

• Event-driven, API-based and batch integration patterns

• CargoWise, logistics or transport-related operations

• Azure, Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, Snowflake or similar technologies

• Advanced analytics, AI or relevant certifications such as TOGAF or DAMA

Why Blue Water

You will become part of a well-established Data Management team with strong professional capabilities across governance, master data, migration and quality.

What characterises the team is not only its expertise, but also its willingness to help each other succeed. We work closely together, challenge each other’s thinking and believe that the best solutions are created through collaboration across business and IT.

As part of the wider Operational Excellence organisation, you will work alongside colleagues specialising in process improvement, training and change management. Together, we are helping Blue Water build the capabilities needed for the future.

Interested?

This is a unique opportunity to help shape the future of data at Blue Water. If you are ready to make a real impact in a global organisation undergoing significant transformation, we would love to hear from you.

For questions about the role, please contact Kamil J. Karolak, Head of Data Management.
